blogs.title: Breaking Free from Tokens
blogs.description: Traditional language models rely on fixed sub-token vocabularies that can mis‑represent rare words or become brittle when input changes—Byte Latent Transformers (BLT) show how training directly on raw bytes keeps the model flexible while still delivering state-of-the-art results.

blogs.title: Patch-Powered Prediction
blogs.description: Introduce blob-based dynamic segmentation where consecutive bytes are grouped into patches based on next-byte entropy estimates, letting BLEP allocate more compute only where data is truly complex.

blogs.title: Cutting Inference Costs by Half
blogs.description: Explain how variable-sized patches mean fewer Transformer steps per input sequence, leading BLT to match functionsally similar token-based models while cutting inference flops up to fifty percent.

blogs.title: "Resilient" Models
blogs.description: "Robustness is everything"—show case studies where BLT outperforms tokenized followers against noisy prompts and demonstrates superior grasp of spelling, phonology and low-resource translation thanks to its byte-level awareness.

blogs.title: "Scaling Without Tokens"
blogs.description: "From Fifty-Fold Data To Eight-Billion Parameters" offers a look at how BLT scales up to 8 B parameters & 4 T training bytes while hitting or beating Llama 3 performance under strictly flop-controlled settings.
